title: A Cipher for the Inheritance
premise: Edmund Blackwood, a night-shift taxi dispatcher with a gift for reading the city's hidden patterns, has quietly solved three deaths the police ruled accidental. When a nervous woman named Vivian Ashcombe pays him in advance to prove her uncle's murder hasn't happened yet, Edmund discovers the old man is already dead — and the family has sealed the case as natural causes. Following a cipher hidden in the uncle's will, Edmund uncovers a dynasty built on laundered money and one forged death certificate from decades ago. In the end, Edmund exposes the killer — the uncle's own heir — but chooses to hand the evidence not to police, who were bought long ago, but to the disinherited granddaughter, letting justice arrive outside the law.
about_author: Cyrus Thackeray spent fifteen years working night dispatch for a metropolitan cab company before turning to fiction, drawing on the strange confessions passengers make at 3 a.m. He lives above a defunct radio repair shop and writes only between midnight and dawn.

chapters.title: The Advance Payment
chapters.summary: Edmund Blackwood, POV. A rain-soaked night shift is interrupted by Vivian Ashcombe, who pays triple rate to have Edmund prove her uncle Gerald won't be murdered before his will is read Friday. When Edmund checks, Gerald died Tuesday — officially of heart failure. The emotional beat is cold dread: Edmund realizes he's been hired to prevent something that has already happened, and someone wanted it that way.

chapters.title: A Will Written in Numbers
chapters.summary: Edmund and Vivian, alternating POV. Breaking into the shuttered Ashcombe house, they find Gerald's real will — a numeric cipher pointing to records from 1974, when Gerald's brother supposedly drowned. The coroner's report is signed by a doctor who never existed. Rising tension: someone ransacked the study hours before them, and Edmund spots the same grey sedan tailing them across two districts.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. The cipher leads to a boathouse and proof that Gerald murdered his brother in 1974 and forged the death certificate — the foundation of the family fortune, now controlled by cousin Marcus Ashcombe, who killed Gerald to bury the secret forever. Climax: Marcus corners Edmund at the boathouse; Vivian arrives armed with the original documents, and Marcus confesses just enough while recording runs.

chapters.title: Justice, Off the Books
chapters.summary: Vivian, POV. Marcus uses his influence to have the evidence dismissed within a day — the police chief owes the Ashcombes everything. Resolution: instead of surrendering the originals, Edmund helps Vivian decode the rest of the cipher, which redirects the entire inheritance to her and funds an independent investigation into the 1974 drowning. The final beat is quiet vindication: the law failed, but the truth found its lawful heir.
